**Finding submitted: deviation (Section 1.4, ¶p0008–p0009), confidence 0.78.**

- **Gap:** The only licence running to us is the Section 1.4 access/right-to-use grant. It names only "the Company" — no affiliates and no contractors/agents (despite the fact that third parties will realistically administer Content and the Site) — and the administration-tool access is limited to the narrow purpose of "monitor[ing] current catalog information." Nothing states the rights are irrevocable, so HDI could arguably suspend or withdraw access outside the Section 4 termination path.
- **Not flagged:** Section 10.3 already carries the agreement to successors and assigns, so no successor-transfer edit was needed; the negotiated one-year renewable term with 90-day notice and Termination Payment was left untouched rather than pushing the "breach-only termination" element of the preferred position, which would be disproportionate to this bargain. The Section 5.4 Marks licence runs from us to HDI and, being appropriately narrow, was left alone.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** adds "its affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf" to both limbs of the grant, broadens tool access to exercising our rights generally, and confirms the rights are irrevocable for the term subject only to Section 4 termination. The comment offers the fallback of adding affiliates on written notice.
